analysis.title: 3Q26 Fundamentals Check-in
key_insights: 3Q26 results so far across IG, HY, and Loan issuers (about 51% reported through November 3) show improving credit fundamentals. Gains are broad based across ratings, unlike the quality-based strength in prior years.
Median quarterly y/y EBITDA growth for current reporters is positive at 9.2% for IG, 9.6% for HY and 8.9% for Loans.
IG leverage fell on both a gross and net basis. Median gross leverage is 2.26x (down 0.04x q/q, 0.06x y/y) and net leverage is 1.61x (down 0.10x q/q, 0.14x y/y). Interest coverage rose to 11.20x.

The gap in gross leverage between BBB and single-A issuers narrowed to 0.5x. BBB leverage improved (2.45x, down 0.09x q/q) while single-A leverage rose (1.96x, up 0.06x q/q). BBBs showed the most consistent improvement across ratings.
IG capex growth y/y is 8.6% in 3Q26, up from 1.9% in 3Q25. Median IG margins are up q/q and y/y (EBITDA margin 24.5%).

By IG sector, Consumer Discretionary had the largest q/q and y/y increase in gross leverage (2.59x, +0.63x q/q, +0.51x y/y). Communication Services had the largest q/q and y/y decline in interest coverage among the sectors MS flagged.

HY credit metrics improved overall across 158 reporters (52% of universe). Gross leverage fell to 3.21x (-0.14x q/q, -0.24x y/y), net leverage to 2.56x, and interest coverage rose to 5.28x. LTM FCF-to-debt rose to 11.8% (+2.5ppt q/q). Only capex-to-sales deteriorated q/q, by less than 0.1ppt.
In HY, 63% of BB issuers have reported versus 36% of single-B. MS notes this mix may flatter metrics until more B issuers report.
By HY rating, BB gross leverage is 2.97x (-0.30x y/y) and B is 3.78x (+0.20x y/y). B interest coverage fell 0.23x y/y to 3.40x, while BB coverage rose 0.23x to 5.72x.
By HY sector, Health Care saw the largest q/q leverage deterioration (+0.31x to 4.18x). Communication Services had the largest ICR improvement (+0.87x to 5.54x).

Leveraged loans (90 reporters, 40% of universe): gross leverage fell 0.23x q/q to 3.43x, 0.13x below a year ago. Net leverage is 2.86x, down 0.20x q/q but still 0.16x above year-ago. Interest coverage is 4.86x.
Loan cash metrics improved: cash-to-debt rose about 2.2ppt q/q to 15.0% and LTM FCF-to-debt rose to 12.4% (+3.45ppt y/y). Only capex-to-sales deteriorated q/q, up about 0.14ppt to 3.95%.
Loan reporting is skewed toward BB (53% reported) versus B (23%) and CCC (21%). MS cautions that CCC (3 issuers) is too small a sample to draw conclusions.
Reported cohorts skew toward higher quality, so metrics will likely change as the remaining reporters come in. MS will publish a complete 3Q26 fundamentals report later.
earnings_insights: Median y/y EBITDA growth for current 3Q26 reporters (about 51% of IG, HY and Loan universes reported through Nov 3): IG 9.2%, HY 9.6%, Loans 8.9%, per the key takeaways summary. The IG exhibit table shows a separate median EBITDA YoY of 12.0% for IG, so the two figures reflect different calculations.
IG current reporters median: sales YoY 7.8%, capex YoY 8.6%, LTM EBITDA margin 23.79%, LTM net income margin 11.78%, LTM FCF margin 7.20%.
HY current reporters median: LTM EBITDA margin 15.9% (+0.5ppt q/q, +0.8ppt y/y), cash-to-debt 12.8%, capex-to-sales 3.8%.
Loan current reporters median: LTM EBITDA margin 19.0%, cash-to-debt 15.0%, capex-to-sales 4.0% (stated as 3.95% in text).
risk_factors: Early read covers only about 51% of companies and is skewed toward higher-quality issuers, so results may change as the season progresses.
Loan net leverage at 2.86x remains 0.16x above year-ago levels.
Single-A IG leverage is rising (+0.06x q/q, +0.19x y/y) and coverage is falling.
Consumer Discretionary IG leverage increased the most among sectors, and Health Care HY leverage rose q/q.
Single-B HY interest coverage is down y/y (3.40x, -0.23x) and the B and CCC cohorts have reported at much lower rates.
